## About the course

This course teaches economics students to work with data the way applied economists do
economists actually do: in code, reproducibly, and with the analysis, the
output and the write-up living in one document.

We start from a blank RStudio window — no prior programming assumed — and
build up through data types, importing messy real-world files, cleaning, and
reshaping with the tidyverse, describing and visualizing data, and finally
writing the whole thing up in Quarto so that a report regenerates itself
When the data changes. Examples use Indian macroeconomic and survey data sets. 


::: {.callout-note}
## Before the first session
Install **R** and then **RStudio**, in that order — both are free.
Lecture 1 walks through the installation screen by screen.

* R — [cran.r-project.org](https://cran.r-project.org/)
* RStudio Desktop — [posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/)
:::

### What you will be able to do

* Set up an R project and keep a piece of work organised and reproducible
* Import data from CSV, Excel and text files, and export results
* Clean, filter, reshape and merge datasets with the tidyverse
* Produce descriptive statistics and publication-quality graphics
* Carry out an exploratory data analysis and defend its conclusions
* Write a report in Quarto that renders to HTML, Word or PDF

## Assessment

The course is assessed by a final project: an exploratory analysis of a
dataset of your choosing, written up in Quarto and submitted as a single
rendered document.

| Resource | |
|:---------|:--|

| [Quarto for Word output — result](<../Rclass_2025/25_Lecture-14_Quarto for Word format.docx>) | The Word file it renders to |
